subject: SLA exposure, latency floor and monthly credit schedule — NovaPilot pilot
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Aurelien Dupont <aurelien@novapilot.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: SLA exposure, latency floor and monthly credit schedule — NovaPilot pilot

Hi Aurelien —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, attaching a working draft of the SLA we propose for the initial 6‑month pilot (SLA_Draft_v3.pdf). High level proposal below so procurement has a concise reference:

- Uptime anchor: 99.65% measured monthly (monthly interval UTC).
- Latency floor: p95 request latency (inference) <= 150ms for US region; latency is measured on production traffic after prefix caching.
- Monthly remedy schedule (credits applied to that month’s invoice):
  * Measured uptime >= 99.65%: no credit.
  * 99.0% <= uptime < 99.65%: 5% invoice credit.
  * 95.0% <= uptime < 99.0%: 12.5% invoice credit.
  * uptime < 95.0%: 25% invoice credit, capped at a monthly maximum credit of 40% of the invoice for that month.
- Latency credits (separate, not cumulative beyond cap): if p95 > 200ms for the month, apply a flat 3% credit; if p95 > 350ms apply 8%. Latency credit counts toward the same monthly cap as uptime credits.
- Exceptions: planned maintenance windows (72‑hour rolling monthly allowance of platform maintenance) and customer‑requested capacity migration windows are excluded from measurement. We propose a 30‑day onboarding measurement carve‑out for traffic pattern learning (metrics recorded but credits not applied).

We included a worked example in Monthly-Credit-worksheet.xlsx to show how a mid‑sized pilot invoice would be adjusted under different scenarios. Think of the anchor as a tradeoff: predictable baseline for both sides while keeping a reasonable cap on exposure.

Ask: can procurement confirm if NovaPilot requires a higher uptime anchor (e.g., 99.8% or 99.9%) or if the primary ask is to reduce the monthly cap on credits? Also please confirm whether EU regional carve‑outs are required up front.

Next steps: if you accept the structure, we’ll circulate a redlineable.docx with tracked items (I’ve asked Karthik to prepare suggested language for maintenance carveouts and regional splits).

Best,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]
[Attachment: Monthly-Credit-worksheet.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)]

From: Aurelien Dupont <aurelien@novapilot.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procureops@novapilot.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 10:11:00 +0200
Subject: Re: SLA exposure, latency floor and monthly credit schedule — NovaPilot pilot

Hi Irene —

Appreciate the detailed starter doc and the worked example. A few quick reactions from procurement and our engineering lead:

1) Anchor level: 99.65% for a production pilot feels low relative to our availability needs. We typically target 99.9% for customer‑facing inference serving. Is there room to push the anchor to 99.8–99.9%?
2) Cap: we like having a cap but 40% of monthly invoice is high for us if a single bad month wipes out the billing. Can we propose a hard cap of 20% for pilots, with a higher cap reserved post‑go‑live?
3) Ramp: we agree to a measured onboarding window but would like the onboarding carve‑out limited to the first 14 days, not 30.
4) Region split: NovaPilot will require explicit EU carveouts — we want the EU‑region SLOs measured and credited separately (billing split is possible).

I'll need to run any revised numbers with finance. Also, please clarify whether the latency metric excludes cold starts and whether the p95 measurement uses synthetic probes or production traffic.

Thanks,
Aurelien

--
Aurelien Dupont
Head of Platform Engineering
NovaPilot
[Contact: aurelien@novapilot.com]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Aurelien Dupont <aurelien@novapilot.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA exposure, latency floor and monthly credit schedule — NovaPilot pilot

Thanks Aurelien — helpful feedback. Quick replies inline and a proposed compromise below:

- Anchor level: we can move to 99.8% for the initial 90‑day pilot if NovaPilot accepts a lower cap on credits for that period (pilot cap 20% of monthly invoice). After the pilot, we can reassess for GA and bump to 99.9% with a separate commercial discussion.
- Cap: agree to reduce pilot cap to 20% as above. Post‑pilot cap can be negotiated based on committed capacity and uptime track record.
- Ramp: we can shorten the onboarding carve‑out to 14 days for credit waivers; metrics will still be collected from day 1 for trending and playbook tuning.
- Region split: we can measure EU region separately for credits. That will require mapping usage to region for billing — our billing team can handle a split invoice if needed.
- Latency measurement: p95 will be calculated on production traffic excluding cold starts; we’ll define cold start as a server instance not used in prior 30 minutes and exclude that sample set. We will record synthetic probe latency for monitoring but only production samples count toward credits.

I’m attaching a short redline checklist (SLA_Redline_comments.docx) with suggested language for the pilot compromise and a clean clause for regional measurement. Karthik / Laura — can one of you review the wording on planned maintenance carveouts to make sure it’s not overly broad?

If NovaPilot signs off on the compromise, we can issue a DocuSign packet with the pilot SLA and the pilot‑stage cap baked in.

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_Redline_comments.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aurelien Dupont <aurelien@novapilot.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA exposure, latency floor and monthly credit schedule — NovaPilot pilot

Thanks Irene / Aurelien — quick operational notes from my side:

- Planned maintenance carveouts: propose a definition limited to pre‑announced maintenance with at least 72 hours’ notice where each tenant’s traffic can be routed off the impacted pool (we do not want an open allowance for unspecified maintenance).
- Measurement mechanics: we will provide a monthly CSV export of per‑region uptime and latency buckets. Our metrics team will also provide the raw query used to compute p95 so NovaPilot can reproduce the result.
- Credit application: credits will be applied to the next invoice and itemized; they will not be automatic refunds to card on file. For transparency, the Monthly‑Credit‑worksheet will be filled out after month close and shared with NovaPilot.

Operational ask for NovaPilot: please confirm the account owner for EU billing mapping and whether NovaPilot prefers a consolidated invoice or two regionally split invoices.

If everyone is aligned I’ll take the redlines and produce an executable draft for DocuSign.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Procurement Team <procureops@novapilot.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurelien Dupont <aurelien@novapilot.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 15:06:00 +0200
Subject: Re: SLA exposure, latency floor and monthly credit schedule — NovaPilot pilot

Team —

We discussed Karthik's operational notes with finance and legal. High‑level confirmation:

- Pilot acceptance: NovaPilot will accept the 99.8% anchor for the 90‑day pilot, with a 20% monthly cap on credits during the pilot.
- Onboarding carve‑out: reduced to 14 days as proposed.
- Planned maintenance: accepted only for pre‑announced events meeting the 72‑hour notice rule and where Redwood provides a mitigation plan.
- Regional invoicing: NovaPilot prefers a single consolidated invoice for now, with regionally itemized line items (EU usage listed separately).

Two small asks before signature:
1) Modify the latency credit trigger: make the lower latency credit threshold p95 > 180ms (rather than 200ms).
2) Add an express limitation that credits are NovaPilot’s sole remedy (no termination right or additional damages during pilot for SLA breaches).

We’ve signed off in principle and can route the DocuSign once those two edits are reflected.

Regards,
NovaPilot Procurement
procureops@novapilot.com

[Note: e‑sign routing will come from legal@novapilot.com after Redwood's revised draft is ready]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Aurelien Dupont <aurelien@novapilot.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA exposure, latency floor and monthly credit schedule — NovaPilot pilot

Great — thank you for the quick review and the clear asks. We will: 

- Update the latency threshold to p95 > 180ms for the lower credit band and keep the higher band at >350ms.
- Add the express remedy limitation to the pilot language (credits are sole and exclusive remedy for pilot stage; termination rights reserved for later contract stage).
- Prepare the final DocuSign packet and PDF (SLA_Final_v1.pdf) and route to the NovaPilot legal e‑sign contact.

I’ll attach the revised PDF and the DocuSign link in the send once the final formatting is set. Karthik / Laura — please confirm you’re good on the final language; I’ll then generate the DocuSign envelope (link below).

DocuSign (draft envelope): https://www.docusign.com/np-sign/abc123

Thanks — look forward to getting the pilot buttoned up.

Irene
